summary: Listed on the Saskatchewan survey at about 54.56 N, 109.60 W, with one observer's listed service 1989-2002; no source describes the site today.

events.note: A towermen list gives one observer's service at Tatakose as 1989 to 2002, with a question mark beside the site name. The entry also notes that the observer went to aerial detection.

evidence.quote: Saskatchewan currently has 42 wildfire detection towers, all equipped with cameras

evidence.supports: The Department of Natural Resources is now called SERM (basis for agency correction)
evidence.quote: Saskatchewan Department Of Natural Resources (now called Saskatchewan Environment and Resource Management or SERM)

corrections.current: Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency (formerly Dept. of Natural Resources)
corrections.why: The survey says the Department of Natural Resources is now called SERM. The Herald report names SPSA as the operator of the 2026 detection towers. No source found links SPSA to the Department, so the 'formerly' clause is unsupported.
The 2013 sources describe a province-wide plan to end observers at 42 towers. None names Tatakose, so 'unstaffed' is not confirmed for this site.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The survey gives coordinates but no height, build year or status. The only site-specific staffing line is one observer's listed service, with a question mark on the site name, so the story presents it as a listing. Observer names are not used (same licence note as Round Hill). The brief's agency and staffing lines are province-wide, not specific to this site. The story is short because the sources are.
